'''Walter Lemon Jr.''' (born July 26, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Shanxi Loongs]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for four years with the [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley Braves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Walt-Lemon,-Jr/Summary/23477|title=Walt Lemon, Jr. Player Profile |publisher=Basketball.realgm.com|accessdate=April 11, 2015}}</ref>

==High school career==
Lemon attended [[Julian High School (Chicago)|Julian High School]] where he averaged 19 points, six assists, five rebounds and three steals per game as a senior, earning him a third-team 3A all-state pick by the Illinois Basketball Coaches Association and a second-team All-Chicago Public League.<ref name="BradleyBio">{{cite web|url=http://www.bradleybraves.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205014633|title=Walt Lemon, Jr. bio|work=BradleyBraves.com|accessdate=November 14, 2015}}</ref><ref>[https://www.nba.com/bulls/gleague/walter-lemon-jr-looks-make-difference-windy-city-bulls-0 WALTER LEMON JR. LOOKS TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE WITH THE WINDY CITY BULLS - “IT’S BEEN ABOUT PLAYING TOGETHER, UNSELFISH BASKETBALL AND THAT HAS TO START WITH ME.” - WALTER LEMON JR.].Retrieved November 14, 2019.</ref><ref>[https://wgntv.com/2019/04/03/walter-lemon-jr-completes-memorable-day-by-helping-the-bulls-to-a-win/ WGN (Chicago) Walter Lemon Jr. completes memorable day by helping the Bulls to a win].Retrieved November 14, 2019.</ref>

==College career==
After graduating, Lemon went to [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley]] between 2010-2014, where he averaged 18 points and 3 rebounds as a senior. When he graduated he ranked among Bradley's all-time top 10 in career points (1721, 7th), assists (367, 10th) and steals (222, 3rd) and had several awards, including the MVC Men's Basketball Scholar-Athlete of the Year in 2014, Bradley's first player ever to win the award.<ref name="BradleyBio" /> He was named to the All‑Missouri Valley Conference Second Team in 2013 and 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=reports |first=Staff |title=High school boys basketball report for February 12 |url=https://www.pjstar.com/story/sports/high-school/2011/02/14/high-school-boys-basketball-report/42185921007/ |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=Peoria Journal Star |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Körmend (2014)===
After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Lemon joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. On September 10, 2014, he signed with Hungarian team [[BC Körmend|EGIS Körmend]] for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/hungary/134270/walter-lemon-jr-signs-with-kormend.html |title=Walter Lemon jr signs with Kormend |work=Sportando.com |date=September 10, 2014 |accessdate=April 11, 2015}}</ref> On December 23, 2014, he parted ways with the club after appearing in 12 league games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/hungary/146035/walter-lemon-jr-leaves-kormend.html |title=Walter Lemon jr. leaves Kormend |work=Sportando.com |date=December 23, 2014 |accessdate=April 11, 2015}}</ref>

===Crailsheim Merlins (2015)===
On February 6, 2015, he signed with the [[Crailsheim Merlins]] of Germany for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Helmstetter |first=Klaus |url=http://www.swp.de/crailsheim/sport/basketball/regional/Hinspiel-Merlins-BBL-Basketball-Rueckspiel-Neuverpflichtung;art5520,3032396 |title=Spiel gegen Trier: Merlins holen Walter Lemon Jr. an Bord |work=Swp.de |date=February 6, 2015 |accessdate=April 11, 2015 |language=German}}</ref> In eight games for the Merlins, he averaged 6.4 points, 1.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game.

===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2015–2016)===
On October 31, 2015, Lemon was selected by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] in the second round of the [[2015 NBA Development League draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.journalgazette.net/blog/mad-antics/Mad-Ants-select--Lemon-9656448|title=Mad Ants select: Lemon|work=JournalGazette.net|date=October 31, 2015|accessdate=October 31, 2015|archive-date=December 12, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151212004451/http://www.journalgazette.net/blog/mad-antics/Mad-Ants-select--Lemon-9656448|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===İstanbulspor Beylikdüzü (2016)===
On July 15, 2016, Lemon signed with İstanbulspor Beylikdüzü of the [[Turkish Basketball First League|TBL]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/454034/Walter-Lemon-Jr.-is-a-newcomer-at-Istanbulspor|title=Walter Lemon Jr. is a newcomer at Istanbulspor|work=Eurobasket.com|date=July 15, 2016|accessdate=September 24, 2016}}</ref>

===Rethymno Cretan Kings (2017)===
On February 20, 2017, Lemon Jr. signed with the Greek team [[Rethymno Cretan Kings B.C.|Rethymno Cretan Kings]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rethymno BC inks Walter Lemon jr|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/226611/rethymno-bc-inks-walter-lemon-jr.html|accessdate=February 20, 2017|date=February 20, 2017}}</ref>

===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2017–2018)===
On November 2, 2017, Lemon was included in the opening night roster for [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Mad Ants Announce 2017-18 Opening Night Roster|url=http://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-announce-2017-18-opening-night-roster/|accessdate=November 2, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2017|archive-date=December 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202151624/http://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-announce-2017-18-opening-night-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Lemon was later named G League Player of the Month for November.<ref>{{cite news|title=Walter Lemon Jr. Named G League Player of the Month|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/walter-lemon-jr-named-g-league-player-month|accessdate=December 1, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2017}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2018)===
On February 21, 2018, the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] signed Lemon to a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pelicans sign Walter Lemon, Jr. to 10-day contract|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-walter-lemon-jr-10-day-contract|accessdate=February 21, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2018}}</ref> He made his NBA debut two days later in a 124–123 overtime win over the [[Miami Heat]], playing in four minutes that night. Lemon signed his second 10-day contract on March 4. After the expiration of his second 10-day contract, Lemon returned to Fort Wayne.<ref>{{cite news|title=Walt Lemon Jr. returns to Fort Wayne|url=http://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/walt-lemon-jr-returns-fort-wayne/|accessdate=March 23, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=March 15, 2018|archive-date=March 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316153412/http://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/walt-lemon-jr-returns-fort-wayne/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Maine Red Claws (2018)===
On July 25, Lemon signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Boston Celtics]]. During this time, he was expected to split his playing time between the Celtics and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Maine Red Claws]]. On November 29, 2018, Lemon was waived by the Celtics without appearing in a game for the parent club.<ref>{{cite web |title=We have waived guard Walt Lemon Jr. |url=https://twitter.com/celtics/status/1068265868386275330 |website=Boston Celtics on Twitter |accessdate=November 29, 2018 |date=November 29, 2018}}</ref>

===Windy City Bulls (2018–2019)===
On December 8, 2018, the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] announced that they had acquired the right of [[Alex Hamilton (basketball)|Alex Hamilton]] and a first round pick in the 2019 NBA G League draft from the [[Windy City Bulls]] in exchange for the right to Lemon.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ryan|last=Stevens|title=Mad Ants Acquire Rights for Alex Hamilton and 2019 Draft Pick|url=https://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-acquire-rights-for-alex-hamilton-and-2019-draft-pick/|accessdate=December 8, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2018}}</ref>

On January 16, 2019, Lemon was suspended for one game without pay and fined for directing inappropriate language toward a game official.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Windy City's Lemon Jr. suspended and fined|url=https://pr.nba.com/windy-citys-lemon-jr-suspended-and-fined/|access-date=October 11, 2021|website=NBA|date=January 16, 2019 }}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2019)===
On March 29, 2019, the [[Chicago Bulls]] announced that they had signed Lemon.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Walt Lemon Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-walt-lemon-jr|date=March 29, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=March 29, 2019}}</ref> On March 30, 2019, Lemon made his debut with the Bulls, scoring 19 points with 6 assists and four steals. In his third game in a Chicago Bulls uniform, in a game against the Wizards in Washington, D.C., on April 3, 2019, Lemon led all players with 24 points in a very efficient 11 of 16 from the floor while leading all players with eight assists. In the final minute of the game, Lemon hit one go ahead basket and afterwards a go-ahead free throw. On the other end of the floor Lemon secured the victory defensively for the Bulls, 115–114.

===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2019–2020)===
On October 10, 2019, the [[Indiana Pacers]] announced that they had signed Lemon.<ref>{{cite web|title=PACERS BRING BACK WALT LEMON JR.|url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/pacers-bring-back-walt-lemon-jr/|date=October 10, 2019|website=SLAM.com|accessdate= October 11, 2019}}</ref> This comes after the release of 2x [[Sun Belt Conference|Sun Belt]] Defensive Player of the Year [[JaKeenan Gant]]. ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2020)===
On August 15, 2020, Lemon signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Hapoel Tel Aviv signs Walter Lemon |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-tel-aviv-signs-walter-lemon/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=August 15, 2020 |date=August 15, 2020 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref> He averaged 10.6 points, 4.2 assists and 1.4 steals per game.<ref name="Ezzahra" />

===Ezzahra Sports (2021)===
On September 11, 2021, Lemon signed with [[Ezzahra Sports]] of the [[Championnat National A]].<ref name="Ezzahra">{{cite news |title=Walt Lemon Jr signs with Ezzahra Sports |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/walt-lemon-jr-signs-with-ezzahra-sports/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 11, 2021 |date=September 11, 2021 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

===Return to the Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2021–2022)===
On December 30, 2021, Lemon signed with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA G League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=December 30, 2021|access-date=December 30, 2021}}</ref> averaging 12.3 points and 6.2 assists in 32 games.<ref name="OttBlackJ">{{cite web|title=BlackJacks Sign NBA Experienced Guard Walter Lemon Jr.|url=https://www.cebl.ca/blackjacks-sign-nba-experienced-guard-walter-lemon-jr|website=CEBL.com|date=May 2, 2022|access-date=May 2, 2022}}</ref>

===Ottawa BlackJacks (2022)===
On May 2, 2022, Lemon signed with the [[Ottawa BlackJacks]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League|CEBL]].<ref name="OttBlackJ" />

=== Club Africain (2022–2023) ===
On September 22, 2022, Lemon signed with [[Club Africain (basketball)|Club Africain]] in Tunisia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Walt Lemon Jr., nouvelle recrue |url=https://clubafricain.com/walt-lemon-jr-nouvelle-recrue/ |website=Site Officiel du CA |access-date=October 19, 2024 |date=September 22, 2022}}</ref>

=== Al-Arabi (2023–2024) ===
In December 2023, Lemon signed with [[Al-Arabi SC (basketball)|Al-Arabi]] of the [[Qatari Basketball League]] (QBL) for the remainder of the 2023–24 season in Qatar.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 17, 2023 |title=Former Bulls player Walt Lemon signed with Qatari team Al-Arabi SC for the remainder of the 2023-24 … |url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/2537369/ |access-date=April 16, 2024 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}}</ref> He guided Al-Arabi to their third Qatari Cup. He scored a game-high 24 points in the final against [[Al Ahli SC (Doha)|Al Ahli Doha]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asian Basketball News, Scores, Stats, Analysis, Standings |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Qatar/news/864139/Al-Arabi-are-2024-Cup-winners |access-date=April 16, 2024 |website=www.asia-basket.com}}</ref>

=== Shanxi Loongs (2024–2025) ===
In December 2024, Lemon signed with the [[Shanxi Loongs]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite web |title=山西男篮再签猛将 |url=http://www.tynews.com.cn/system/2024/12/22/030836682.shtml |website=太原新闻网-太原日报社 |access-date=December 27, 2024 |date=December 22, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is the son of Walter Sr. and Katrina Lemon and is one of three siblings. Earning a spot on the Bradley Athletic Director's Honor Roll three times, Lemon earned his bachelor's degree in psychology.<ref name="BradleyBio" />
